newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippine '97 coconut oil exports seen up 60 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine '97 coconut oil exports seen up 60 pct.

text.p: Philippine coconut oil exports in calendar 1997 are seen rising nearly 60 percent to around 1.3 million tonnes against 813,157 tonnes in 1996, the president of the Coconut Oil Refiners Association (CORA) said on Thursday.

CORA President Jesus Arranza said coconut oil production should bounce back after plunging more than 40 percent last year when a string of typhoons late in 1995 knocked down 300,000 coconut trees and sharply curtailed production.
"It began raining early this year and that should help the nuts on the coconut trees mature," Arranza told Reuters in an interview at the Third Edible Oil Markets conference in Singapore.
"We are hoping that it (total coconut oil exports) will reach 1.2-1.3 million tonnes this year," he added.
The Philippines is the world's leading producer of coconut products.
